sure if thats right". He was right on both, and the paper that says so was already on this disk.
EVERY NUMBER IN THIS COMMENT WAS COMPUTED, and the command is named. A number in a comment that
nothing recomputes is a rumour, and the file this replaced was 124 lines of them.
WHAT THE WEEK IS
Monday     box jump, heavy back squat 5-7, Bulgarian split squat, trunk and grip   4 blocks, 23 sets
Tuesday    lat pulldown fresh, heavy RDL 6-8, front squat, calves and trunk        4 blocks, 24 sets
Thursday   DB bench press LEADING, overhead press, single-leg RDL, back squat 8     4 blocks, 24 sets
Friday     lateral bound, Bulgarian split squat, heavy BB row, trunk, RDL 8         5 blocks, 27 sets
ORDER IS A STRENGTH VARIABLE AND NOT A SIZE VARIABLE, which is the finding the whole rebuild
turns on. Nunes 2021 (PMID 32077380, sources/pubmed-32077380.txt), eleven good-to-excellent
studies: starting with the multi-joint exercise favours strength in that exercise (ES 0.32,
p = 0.034) and order has no effect on hypertrophy (ES 0.03, p = 0.862). So position in the
session is a prescription. There was no instrument for it in this repo until now:
`scripts/gym-order.mjs` asserts every pattern gets a slot in the first two blocks of some day.
THE PROGRAMME THIS REPLACED FAILS THAT CHECK on single-leg and on chest. Chest was a partner in
all three of its appearances, never a lead, never in block 1 or 2. That is what he noticed.
THE SESSION IS SHORTER ON THE MEASURE THAT OWNS THE CLOCK, and the honest version of that claim is
narrower than the one this file carried until 2026-09-01. It read "this is the one claim he can check
against his own watch", and two lines below it gave Friday a range of 60 to 108 minutes against the old
programme's watch-measured 90th percentile of 100. So the pessimistic end of the new longest day is
LONGER than the old bad days, and the claim only holds if the pairing really is free. That assumption
is what validate.mjs now checks the arithmetic of, and it is not the same thing as having measured it
on him. What is certain is the lead-set count, 76 to 53, because those are the sets nothing rides
inside. Whether the total lands near the floor or the ceiling is his watch to settle, not this file's.
prescribed sets per week      121 before  ->   98 now
sets that OWN THE CLOCK        76 before  ->   53 now
The second row is the real one. A block is a lead plus a partner that rides in the lead rest, and
`validate.mjs` now refuses a pair where the partner does not actually fit in the gap the lead
offers, computed from sets, reps and rest. It caught two calf blocks in this rebuild: 135 seconds
of gap against 180 seconds of work. So only the lead sets add wall-clock time.
On the 23 days where the watch and the app both have data he spent 4.0 minutes per set he logged.
At that rate Day 1 is 68 to 116 minutes and Day 4 is 36 to 72; the low end assumes the pairing is
free and the high end assumes it buys nothing. His watch says 70 minutes at the median over the
last 90 days and 100 at the 90th percentile, measured on the LONGER programme this replaces.
THE PRIORITY LIFTS ARE GETTING LESS VOLUME ON PURPOSE, and this is the part that reads backwards.
Pelland Table 4 is STRENGTH, denominated per assessed EXERCISE, and stops finding detectable
increments at about 4 fractional weekly sets. Table 3 is HYPERTROPHY, per MUSCLE, scale 4 to 42.
They are not interchangeable and this project graded strength against the hypertrophy table for a
day. `scripts/gym-strength.mjs` is the strength half. Measured against the accepted baseline:
BB Back Squat          19.5 -> 20.5      Single-Leg RDL     17.5 -> 16
Bulgarian Split Squat    19 -> 20.5      Front Squat        14.5 -> 14.5
BB Romanian Deadlift     18 -> 17.5      DB Lateral Lunge     16 -> 14.5
sum past the point of detectable increments: 112.0 -> 79.5
Every priority lift moved DOWN toward the number the evidence points at. It is still far past it,
and that is a cost the gate prints rather than a fault it fails, because Pelland 4.3 says
"additional sets beyond this point may produce additional strength gains, albeit less than the
SDES". Past 4 is a price, not a wall, and a fabricated ceiling in this repo has already been used
once to refuse dozens of legal exercises.
AND THE COUNTING IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE, which is why a mid-rebuild instinct to loosen the gate was
wrong. Nearly every lower-body lift here shares the glutes, so fractional volume for ANY of them
is dominated by the total count of lower-body sets in the week. Raising frequency raises it
mechanically. A draft with 52 lower sets against the live 47 pushed every priority lift UP; the
gate was right and the draft was wrong. Cutting to 38 brought all five down.
WHAT SHOULDER WORK USED TO DO TO THE FRONT OF A LOWER DAY. The programme this replaces opened one
lower day with five sets of lateral bound, then three of DB lateral raise, and only reached the
barbell RDL at set nine. Side delts also carried 4.9 times the chest volume. Removing a partner
makes its lead a solo lift, so this was a rearrangement and not a deletion.
THE ARMS GET ONE DIRECT SLOT EACH, deliberately. `scripts/gym-targets.mjs` grades every muscle
against a band in `content/gym/targets.json`. The presses already deliver 6 fractional triceps
sets and the pulls 3 biceps sets before any curl or extension exists, so two direct slots each
put both at 12 against a maintenance band of 4-10. One each puts both at 9.
THE TRUNK IS GRADED ON PRESENCE, NOT ON A RATIO, and the reason is written at `minDirectSets` in
targets.json. Every trunk number here is another lift secondary work: erectors get 10.5 from the
squat, the RDL and the row with no direct erector exercise in the week at all, and abs get 3 from
the front squat and the overhead press. A spread cap across that region cannot be satisfied by
any programme anyone would write, and a spread cap on all fractional sets passes a week with
every dead bug deleted. Both were measured. The floor on direct sets catches it and they do not.
WHAT COULD NOT BE FIXED, and it is the honest limit on everything above.
DELIVERY IS PRICED PER EXERCISE FROM HIS OWN LOG, `scripts/gym-delivered.mjs`, and 38 prescribed
lower-body sets price out at 30.9 to 37.2 delivered. Two rates, neither of them the truth: the
ceiling is done rows over rows that exist and cannot see a session he never opened, the floor
counts a whole uncaptured session as a total miss. 33 app days against 56 watch sessions says he
does not log everything, so a claim that needs the ceiling is a claim resting on an assumption
this project has already measured to be false.
TWO EXERCISES HERE HAVE TWO LOGGED SETS EACH: the DB calf raise and the DB reverse fly. He did
both within three days of this rebuild, so they are treated as his rather than as things he
skips, but the log cannot price them and the gate says so rather than filling them with an
average. Filling a thin exercise with the population average is exactly what inflated an earlier
"+56% delivered lower-body work" headline.
PERFORMED MEANS `done = true OR reps > 0`, everywhere, and it is defined once in
`src/lib/gym/db.ts`. Ticking the circle is a separate gesture from typing the numbers and 66 of
646 rows carry real reps with done = false. `gym_session.sets_prescribed` is the only honest
completion denominator.
THE GATES, and what each one refuses. Run `node scripts/verify.mjs` before pushing.
content/gym/validate.mjs        shape, stations, walking route, verbatim whyHere, block fit
scripts/gym-order.mjs           every pattern gets a fresh slot (Nunes)
scripts/gym-strength.mjs        Table 4 per priority lift, against a dated baseline
scripts/gym-targets.mjs         Table 3 per muscle, bands and direct-work floors
scripts/gym-coverage.mjs        below-minimum, strict pairings, unsourced, against a baseline
scripts/check-ladder.mjs        does maxing the rep range earn the next weight (needs Neon)
scripts/gym-delivered.mjs       what this will actually deliver (needs Neon)
HealthOS/knowledge/check-sources.mjs   every citation resolves and none is a dropped source
THREE OF THOSE FOUND THEIR OWN FIRST BUG ON THEIR FIRST RUN. gym-targets invented two findings
for muscles the catalogue does not define. gym-order lumped chest with front delts and PASSED the
candidate. And check-sources had two invisible backspace bytes baked into a regex by a bad
escape, so it could match nothing and reported three false positives out of three. A gate that
has only ever been seen to pass has not been seen to work; all three have now been watched
refusing.
CONDITIONING IS NOT IN THIS FILE. It lives in conditioning.json. The swim follows the lift on the
same evening, which is the constraint that makes session length a prescription rather than a
preference.
HIS EMAIL ANSWERS, 2026-09-01, AND WHAT THEY CHANGED. Verbatim in HealthOS/comms/questions.jsonl
under id gym-redesign-3. He answered by voice, so the text runs on. He rejected the premise of all
three questions and was right all three times.
THE DAYS ARE EVEN NOW, 23/24/24/27, and were 29/24/24/18. The short Friday existed so a tight swim
gap had somewhere easy to land. He killed the reason: "the stream is always right after the lift, so
I don't think that's case enough to say oh I'm doing this deliberate." The gap is not a property of
one day, so designing one day around it was circular. Measured the same day from 140 sessions where
the watch caught a lift and then a swim: the gap runs a median of 19 minutes, a quarter of them
under 13, and its correlation with how long the lift ran is r = 0.14. A longer lift does not squeeze
the gap. He was right and the instrument agrees.
THE HEAVY REP RANGES ARE HIS OWN LOGGED ONES. Squat 5 to 7, RDL 6 to 8. He said "I feel like we
should stay where we are... I'm more worried on keeping my form and maybe improving on that than
going heavier", and he knows the cost: "I also know that does gonna kind of hinder my progression."
Those ranges are not a compromise, they are the three rep counts he actually performs: squat 5 on 9
sets, 6 on 9, 7 on 8; RDL 6 on 16 sets, 8 on 9. A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the email that asked him
said the heavy lifts had been "4 to 6 reps, not 8". They were never 8. The card said 5 for the squat
and 6 for the RDL before the rebuild, so the change he objected to was one rep, not three.
AND THE EVIDENCE IS ON HIS SIDE MORE THAN THE QUESTION IMPLIED. See
HealthOS/knowledge/sources/LOAD-VS-REPS-AND-OVERLOAD-2026-09-01.md. Heavier is not the only route:
Iversen 2021 reports 1RM increases of 35% heavy against 28% light. Not having to add load every
session is the better-evidenced structure, not a concession: Moesgaard 2022 finds undulating beats
linear for 1RM in trained lifters, ES 0.61. And a large part of strength is not muscle at all,
Dankel: "Increases in 1RM strength ... are likely driven by mechanisms other than muscle growth",
which means the form work he wants to prioritise is a strength mechanism and not a consolation.
NOTHING HERE MAY CITE ESTIMATED 1RM TO HIM AS A FACT ABOUT HIS BODY: all 114 saved papers were
grepped for Epley and Brzycki on 2026-09-01 and there are ZERO hits, so check-ladder.mjs is an
internal consistency check on an unvalidated model. Its header now says so.
TWO EXERCISES CAME BACK BECAUSE THE REBUILD DELETED THEM BY MISTAKE, and he spotted the class of it
without seeing the diff: "there's still I feel exercises that are not even in the list for some
reason. I don't want to have to point to an exercise." The lateral bound was on Thursday and he
performed it 2026-08-30, THE DAY BEFORE the rebuild dropped it. The DB lateral lunge was on Monday,
loadable, direct adductors, and its cue opens "This is the sideways movement you asked for". The
rebuild moved the bound off the front of a lower day, which was right, and then deleted it instead
of relocating it. That is the C3 violation the brief named: removing a partner makes its lead solo,
which is a REARRANGEMENT and not a deletion. Until they came back the week had ZERO direct abductor
or sideways work in all 16 blocks, while equipment.json cites Comert and Gruber 2025 for loaded
frontal-plane work as the replacement for the banded walks that were cut, and that replacement had
never shipped.
THE COST OF PUTTING THEM BACK, stated because it is real: the back squat and the split squat moved
from 17.5 to 20.5 fractional strength sets, above where the OLD programme had them. Nearly every
lower-body lift here shares the glutes, so any lower-body set raises all of their fractional counts.
It was accepted because both sit about 16 sets past the point where Pelland stops finding detectable
increments, so 17.5 against 20.5 is noise on the outcome axis, while the sideways work was the only
thing covering a direction nothing else trains. The real price is the clock: 95 sets to 98, about 12
minutes a week at his measured rate. strength-baseline.json carries the full reasoning and the
condition that would make it the wrong call.
WHY THERE IS STILL NO HIP THRUST, since he asked by name. It IS in the catalogue, as smith-hip-thrust,
and it IS loadable. It is excluded on evidence that is saved and was read directly rather than
trusted from a note: Plotkin 2023 (sources/plotkin-2023-hip-thrust.html) trained hip thrust against
back squat and found "Gluteus mCSA increases were similar across both groups", with the point

greater mCSA growth for quadriceps ... and adductors". He squats twice a week. So the hip thrust
would not add glute growth the squat is not already producing, and the squat brings quads and
adductors it does not. A CUE FOR IT IS NOW WRITTEN ANYWAY, drafted from that paper's own methods and
labelled a draft in the text he reads, so adding it is one word from him rather than a session of
work. What the paper also shows, and what nothing here covers well, is that gluteus medius and
minimus grew LEAST in both groups.
THE SWAP CONTROL CAN REACH FIVE GROUPS IT PHYSICALLY COULD NOT BEFORE. scripts/gym-alts.mjs only
walked the movement group of each prescribed slot, so any group with no prescribed member was
invisible however good its cue: hip-extension-isolation, knee-flexion, adduction, hip-abduction and
plyo-lateral were all in that state. His complaint about exercises "not even in the list" was
literally caused by that. A candidate now qualifies if every one of its primary movers is also a

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.cue: THREE JUMPS A SET, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SET. Not as many as you can: three, then stop and rest. This is the one exercise here where being tired makes it worse rather than better, because what you are training is how fast you leave the floor, and the fourth jump is always slower than the first. A slow jump is just a squat you did standing up. Five sets of three is fifteen jumps, and every one of them should feel like the first. HOW TO DO IT. Stand a forearm's length from the box. Swing the arms back, bend the knees about a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. Then STEP down one foot at a time, never jump down. Success looks like: you hear almost nothing when you land, and you could hold the landing still for two seconds. If you land with a thud or stumble, the box is too high. If the third jump feels slower than the first, rest longer before the next set rather than pushing through.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

alts.name: Lateral Bound
alts.cue: THREE OR FOUR BOUNDS A SIDE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SET. Not as many as you can. Same reason as the box jump on Monday: what you are training is how hard you can push off in one go, and a tired bound is a slow bound, which trains something else. More work means more SETS. HOW TO DO IT. Replaces the broad jump, which you swapped out every single time. This is the sideways explosive work you asked for. Stand on your LEFT leg. Push off it sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE completely still for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over your toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and freeze. Success looks like: silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop to catch yourself. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.

alts.name: Clamshell
alts.cue: On your side, short band above the knees, knees bent 90. Open the top knee like a clam without letting your hips roll backwards. Success looks like: your top hip stays stacked over the bottom one. If you have to roll back to open further, you have gone as far as it goes. 3x15 each side.

blocks.why: Jumps first, while fresh, and nothing rides alongside: a jump needs clear floor and a partner takes it. Deng 2024 reports small to moderate effects across four outcomes at 2 to 3 sessions a week, none of them individually significant, which is why this is on two days rather than four and why it is not the point of the day.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Back Squat

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if you were pouring from two jugs. Lower slowly, about twice as long coming down as going up. Success looks like: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top instead of it swinging. If either fails, go lighter. This is the SIDE of the shoulder, and it is the one thing nothing else in the week trains: every press works the front, every row works the back. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: DB Lateral Raise goes in the rest because the BB Back Squat does not use them.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

blocks.why: The heavy squat of the week and the one that gets progressed. Four to six reps, because Pelland Table 4 stops finding detectable strength increments past about four fractional sets a lift and load is the lever that is left. DB Lateral Raise goes in the rest because the BB Back Squat does not use them.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

exercises.name: DB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there, like you are pinching a pencil between them. Breathe in, lower the dumbbells until you feel a good stretch across the chest, PAUSE for one second so there is no bounce, then press up and breathe out. The dumbbells travel slightly toward each other at the top but do not clang. ADDED 2026-08-22, after he reported feeling this mostly in the triceps and the front of the shoulder: that is usually where the dumbbells are travelling, not how hard you are pushing. Two things to try. Before the first rep, pull your shoulder blades DOWN and TOGETHER into the bench and keep them pinned there the whole set, so your chest is the highest point and the shoulders cannot roll forward. Then press over your LOWER chest, not your collarbone: at the bottom the dumbbells should be beside your nipples with your elbows about halfway between tucked-in and straight-out, and at the top they finish above the same spot rather than drifting toward your face. Success looks like: at the bottom you feel a stretch across the chest, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder. This is standard coaching practice, not a trial finding.
exercises.whyHere: DB Bench Press goes in the rest because the Bulgarian Split Squat does not use the chest.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: Your second press of the week, moderate rather than heavy: Tuesday is the day the bench gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Lean your chest forward to bias the chest. Enough counterweight for 8 clean reps. You had 5 strict dips in May, so this is trackable.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat, dumbbells. About 30 degrees, which is one or two notches, not half way up. More work for the top of the chest and the front of the shoulder, less for the middle and lower chest. Your note #31 asked what the difference is: neither is better, they are different halves of the same muscle, and the steeper you go the more the shoulder takes over. Success looks like: you feel it across your collarbone rather than under your nipple line. If your shoulders are doing all of it, lower the bench a notch. If you are doing this instead of flat, SWAP TO IT on the card so your log says what you actually pressed.

alts.name: Chest Fly Machine
alts.cue: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.

blocks.why: Single-leg strength, in a main block rather than an accessory one, which is where every one of his single-leg sets sits today. DB Bench Press goes in the rest because the Bulgarian Split Squat does not use the chest.

blocks.label: Trunk and Grip

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the bench, between press sets. Your example, and it is the pairing that always worked. On your back, arms straight up at the ceiling, knees bent up over your hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and keep it there: that is the entire exercise. Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathe out as they go. Stop the moment your lower back lifts off the floor, even if the leg is nowhere near down. Come back and swap sides.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Hanging Knee Raise
alts.cue: Hang from the pull-up bar on top of the rack with your arms straight and your feet clear of the floor. Bring both knees up towards your chest until your thighs pass level, then lower them under control until your legs are straight again. Success looks like: you come to a stop at the bottom before the next rep, so every one starts from still rather than from a swing. If you are swinging, do fewer. THIS CUE IS A DRAFT: it was written for you rather than taken off a published page, and nobody has read it standing at the bar. Say what it should say.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: Done after the curls rather than alternating with them, because it needs room to walk and the preacher seat does not travel. A heavy dumbbell in each hand, stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Grip, posture and everything down your sides at once. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after. COUNT SECONDS, and type the seconds. Start the watch before you pick the dumbbells up, because you cannot press anything with both hands full. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.
exercises.whyHere: Farmer Carry goes in the rest because the Dead Bug does not use the grip.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, and THE RACK STOPS AT 50 LB EACH: that is the whole set, 20 up to 50, two of each. His note #18, 2026-08-25: 'Therea no kettlebell after 50 for farmers'. He is right, and it is why the prescribed version is dumbbells, which go to 90 and which he has already carried at 75 per hand. alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

blocks.why: The trunk braced under load, and the grip that limits the RDL before the hamstrings do. Farmer Carry goes in the rest because the Dead Bug does not use the grip.

blocks.label: Vertical Pull

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

exercises.name: DB Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, roughly halfway to parallel with the floor, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang straight below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: DB Reverse Fly goes in the rest because the Lat Pulldown only catches the rear delts on the way through, and this is the one thing here that trains them on purpose.

alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the adjustable cable column, standing tall, a handle in each hand and a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

blocks.why: The upper pull Iversen names as a minimum, and it leads because Nunes found the strength gain is largest in whatever is performed first. It has never had a fresh slot in this programme. blocks.label: Main Lift: Romanian Deadlift

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge, the one we progress. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar stays touching your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and then FREEZE them, then push your hips backward toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and snap the hips forward to stand up, breathing out at the top. If your lower back rounds you have gone too far down. STRAPS, because you asked on 18 August: yes, use them, and they will not cost you anything here. Do the first warm-up set with bare hands so you keep noticing what your grip is doing, then strap up for all four working sets. The hamstrings are what this lift is for, and stopping a set because the bar is slipping out of your fingers trains neither. Your grip is not being neglected either: the Farmer Carry on Friday and the Suitcase Carry on Monday are both held bare-handed and that is where grip is meant to be worked. This is standard coaching practice rather than something a trial has tested, so it is a convention, not evidence.

alts.name: Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: Has sat at 40 lb since May, so this time the weight moves, not just the reps. One dumbbell in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and frozen. Push the hip backward and let the free leg extend straight behind you like a see-saw, keeping your hips square to the floor: the back hip must not open toward the ceiling. Go until you feel the hamstring stretch, then stand and squeeze. Slow. Touch the bench with your free toe if you lose balance.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if you were pouring from two jugs. Lower slowly, about twice as long coming down as going up. Success looks like: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top instead of it swinging. If either fails, go lighter. This is the SIDE of the shoulder, and it is the one thing nothing else in the week trains: every press works the front, every row works the back. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: DB Lateral Raise goes in the rest because the BB Romanian Deadlift does not use them.

alts.name: KB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

blocks.why: The heavy hinge of the week and his most reliable lift: 185 lb, 34 logged sets, every one completed. (Not 225. The 225 in this file until 2026-09-01 came from 2026-08-05, which movements.json already records as a conventional deadlift logged under the RDL by mistake.) Four to six reps for the same reason as the squat. DB Lateral Raise goes in the rest because the BB Romanian Deadlift does not use them.

blocks.label: Squat

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: BB Back Squat
alts.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

alts.name: Smith Squat
alts.cue: On rails. Feet slightly forward of the bar. Same depth, no balance demand.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the bench, between press sets. Your example, and it is the pairing that always worked. On your back, arms straight up at the ceiling, knees bent up over your hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and keep it there: that is the entire exercise. Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathe out as they go. Stop the moment your lower back lifts off the floor, even if the leg is nowhere near down. Come back and swap sides.
exercises.whyHere: Dead Bug goes in the rest because the Front Squat braces the trunk hard and never moves it, and this is the one thing here that makes it work through a range.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Hanging Knee Raise
alts.cue: Hang from the pull-up bar on top of the rack with your arms straight and your feet clear of the floor. Bring both knees up towards your chest until your thighs pass level, then lower them under control until your legs are straight again. Success looks like: you come to a stop at the bottom before the next rep, so every one starts from still rather than from a swing. If you are swinging, do fewer. THIS CUE IS A DRAFT: it was written for you rather than taken off a published page, and nobody has read it standing at the bar. Say what it should say.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

blocks.why: The second squat, a different lift rather than a lighter copy of the heavy one. Dead Bug goes in the rest because the Front Squat braces the trunk hard and never moves it, and this is the one thing here that makes it work through a range.

blocks.label: Calves and Trunk

exercises.name: DB Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Standing on the floor in the rest between lunge sets, a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides. Feet about hip width. Push all the way up onto your toes, as high as you can go, and hold for one second at the top. Then lower slowly, about three seconds down, until your heels touch the floor and you feel a stretch through the back of the calf. Success looks like: you can hold the top position still for a second without wobbling, and the slow way down is what you feel most. If you cannot hold the top, the dumbbells are too heavy. This is the flat-floor version, so the stretch at the bottom is smaller than on the machine; that is the trade for it costing you no walk.

alts.cue: On the standing calf machine. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

exercises.cue: Done after the curls rather than alternating with them, because it needs room to walk and the preacher seat does not travel. A heavy dumbbell in each hand, stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Grip, posture and everything down your sides at once. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after. COUNT SECONDS, and type the seconds. Start the watch before you pick the dumbbells up, because you cannot press anything with both hands full. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.

alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

blocks.why: The calves, which carry the lowest loaded volume in the programme, and the trunk under load. Farmer Carry goes in the rest because the DB Calf Raise does not use the grip.

blocks.label: Horizontal Press

exercises.name: DB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there, like you are pinching a pencil between them. Breathe in, lower the dumbbells until you feel a good stretch across the chest, PAUSE for one second so there is no bounce, then press up and breathe out. The dumbbells travel slightly toward each other at the top but do not clang. Before the first rep, pull your shoulder blades DOWN and TOGETHER into the bench and keep them pinned there the whole set, so your chest is the highest point and the shoulders cannot roll forward. Then press over your LOWER chest, not your collarbone: at the bottom the dumbbells should be beside your nipples with your elbows about halfway between tucked-in and straight-out, and at the top they finish above the same spot rather than drifting toward your face. Success looks like: at the bottom you feel a stretch across the chest, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder. This is standard coaching practice, not a trial finding.

alts.cue: Your second press of the week, moderate rather than heavy: Tuesday is the day the bench gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Lean your chest forward to bias the chest. Enough counterweight for 8 clean reps. You had 5 strict dips in May, so this is trackable.

alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat, dumbbells. About 30 degrees, which is one or two notches, not half way up. More work for the top of the chest and the front of the shoulder, less for the middle and lower chest. Your note #31 asked what the difference is: neither is better, they are different halves of the same muscle, and the steeper you go the more the shoulder takes over. Success looks like: you feel it across your collarbone rather than under your nipple line. If your shoulders are doing all of it, lower the bench a notch. If you are doing this instead of flat, SWAP TO IT on the card so your log says what you actually pressed.

alts.name: Chest Fly Machine
alts.cue: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.

exercises.name: DB Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Standing on the floor in the rest between lunge sets, a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides. Feet about hip width. Push all the way up onto your toes, as high as you can go, and hold for one second at the top. Then lower slowly, about three seconds down, until your heels touch the floor and you feel a stretch through the back of the calf. exercises.whyHere: DB Calf Raise goes in the rest because the DB Bench Press does not use the calves.

alts.name: Machine Calf Raise
alts.cue: On the standing calf machine. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

blocks.why: The DB Bench Press leads a block for the first time. He asked about this directly: it has been a partner in every appearance, never fresh, and Nunes found order costs strength and not size. DB Calf Raise goes in the rest because the DB Bench Press does not use the calves.

blocks.label: Overhead Press

exercises.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
exercises.cue: STANDING, not seated: that is the difference between this and the seated version in the alternatives, and it is why this needs no bench. Done second in the session from 2026-08-22, and the reason is in "Why this is here". Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs do not flare and your lower back does not arch. Press straight up until the arms are locked out with the dumbbells over the middle of your head, not in front of your face. Lower under control to the shoulders. Success looks like: your ribs stay down and you can hold the lockout still for a second. If your back arches to start the rep, go lighter.

alts.name: Machine Shoulder Press
alts.cue: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not above your ears. Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging, and come back down slowly until the handles are level with your shoulders again. Stop the set when your lower back starts arching off the pad.

alts.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Press
alts.cue: One knee down, the other foot forward, one dumbbell in the hand on the SAME side as the down knee. Press it straight overhead without letting your ribs flare or your body lean away. It is two exercises at once: a press, and your trunk refusing to bend sideways under a load held on one side. Lighter than the two-dumbbell version by a lot, and that is the point.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, back supported. Takes the lower back out of it entirely.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Standing, one dumbbell held in both hands behind your head, elbows pointing up and staying pointed up. Straighten your arms to lift the weight overhead without letting your elbows drift out sideways. Lower until you feel a stretch under the arm. Success looks like: your elbows stay in the same place the whole set and only your forearms move. If your elbows flare, go lighter.
exercises.whyHere: DB Overhead Tricep Extension goes in the rest because the Seated DB Overhead Press finishes with the triceps rather than starting with them, and this is the one thing here that loads them directly.

open.q: You said you would rather do assisted dips than pushdowns. The pushdown is gone from the week, so this overhead extension is the only direct triceps work left, and swapping in the dip would move this block to the machine bank, which nothing else on this day visits. Do you want the dip here?

alts.name: Tricep Pushdown
alts.cue: Cable high, rope or straight bar. Pin your elbows to your sides and keep them there: only the forearms move. Push down until the arms are completely straight, hold half a second, then let it come up slowly until you feel the stretch. If your elbows drift forward or you lean over the bar, drop the weight.

alts.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the high pulley. Take the handle overhead, then bend only your elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel a stretch down the back of your arms, about level with the base of your skull. Your upper arms stay pointing at the ceiling and DO NOT drift forward: that is the whole exercise. Straighten the arms to come back up. Success looks like: your elbows stay the same distance apart the whole time and your ribs do not flare forward. If your back arches, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: DB Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the elbow to lower them beside your ears and press back up. Use this if overhead bothers your shoulder.

alts.name: EZ Bar Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench with the EZ bar. Keep the upper arms still and pointing at the ceiling, bend only at the elbow to lower the bar toward your forehead, then straighten. Light.

blocks.why: The upper push at the shoulder, 65 lb over 23 logged sets, and it leads block two so it gets the fresh slot Nunes says the strength gain lives in. It was deleted from the previous candidate without a record. DB Overhead Tricep Extension goes in the rest because the Seated DB Overhead Press finishes with the triceps rather than starting with them, and this is the one thing here that loads them directly.

blocks.label: Single-Leg Hinge

Push the hip backward and let the free leg extend straight behind you like a see-saw, keeping your hips square to the floor: the back hip must not open toward the ceiling. Go until you feel the hamstring stretch, then stand and squeeze. Slow. Touch the bench with your free toe if you lose balance.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

alts.name: KB Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: Same movement holding a kettlebell. The handle sits closer to your leg, which some people find easier to control. 8/leg.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

alts.cue: Lying or seated depending on which machine is free. Set the pad so it sits just ABOVE your heels, on the Achilles, not on your calf. Lie or sit with your knees lined up with the machine pivot, the bolt the arm turns on. Curl your heels toward your bum as far as the machine allows, pause for one second at the tightest point, then lower slowly, taking about twice as long down as up. Success looks like: your hips stay flat on the pad and do not lift as you curl. If they lift, go lighter. This is the only exercise in the week that bends the knee against resistance: every other hamstring movement here is a hinge, where the hamstring works at the hip instead. exercises.name: DB Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, roughly halfway to parallel with the floor, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang straight below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. alts.name: Cable Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. At the adjustable cable column, standing tall, a handle in each hand and a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

blocks.why: One leg at a time on the hinge, where balance is the limit before load is. DB Reverse Fly goes in the rest because the Single-Leg RDL does not use them.

exercises.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: DB Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging by your sides, palms facing IN toward your thighs and STAYING that way the whole rep: that is what makes it a hammer curl instead of a normal curl. Pin your elbows against your ribs. Bend the elbow and bring the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, then lower it all the way until the arm is straight. Success looks like: your elbows have not travelled forward and your body has not swung to start the rep. If it swings, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: DB Hammer Curl goes in the rest because the BB Back Squat does not use the arms.

alts.name: DB Biceps Curl
alts.cue: Standing, dumbbells, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.

alts.name: Cable Curl
alts.cue: Low cable with a straight or EZ attachment. The cable keeps tension on the muscle at every point, including the top where dumbbells go light. 3x12.

alts.name: Incline DB Curl
alts.cue: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

alts.name: Kettlebell Curl
alts.cue: A kettlebell in each hand by the handle, same elbow-pinned curl. The weight hangs behind your hand, which makes the top half harder.

blocks.why: The third squat exposure of the week, at a higher rep range than the heavy day. DB Hammer Curl goes in the rest because the BB Back Squat does not use the arms.

friday.name: Friday
friday.title: Friday: single leg fresh, pull heavy

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.cue: THREE OR FOUR BOUNDS A SIDE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SET. Not as many as you can. Same reason as the box jump on Monday: what you are training is how hard you can push off in one go, and a tired bound is a slow bound, which trains something else. More work means more SETS. HOW TO DO IT. Replaces the broad jump, which you swapped out every single time. This is the sideways explosive work you asked for. Stand on your LEFT leg. Push off it sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE completely still for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over your toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and freeze. Success looks like: silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop to catch yourself. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Box Jump
alts.cue: THREE JUMPS A SET, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SET. Not as many as you can: three, then stop and rest. This is the one exercise here where being tired makes it worse rather than better, because what you are training is how fast you leave the floor, and the fourth jump is always slower than the first. A slow jump is just a squat you did standing up. Five sets of three is fifteen jumps, and every one of them should feel like the first. HOW TO DO IT. Stand a forearm's length from the box. Swing the arms back, bend the knees about a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. Then STEP down one foot at a time, never jump down. Success looks like: you hear almost nothing when you land, and you could hold the landing still for two seconds. If you land with a thud or stumble, the box is too high. If the third jump feels slower than the first, rest longer before the next set rather than pushing through.

alts.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
alts.cue: On the floor. Lie on your back, one heel planted close to your butt, the other leg lifted and held straight out. Push through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knee to shoulder, then lower slowly. Success looks like: you feel it in the back of the planted thigh and the butt cheek, not in your lower back. If you feel your lower back, your hips went too high. 3x12 each side.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Lateral Line Hop
alts.cue: The easier version. Both feet together, hop side to side over a line on the floor, small and fast, staying on the balls of your feet. 3x15.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds at the widest point, then let them come back slowly. Success looks like: you feel it on the outside of the hip, above and behind the hip bone. 3x15.

alts.name: Clamshell
alts.cue: On your side, short band above the knees, knees bent 90. Open the top knee like a clam without letting your hips roll backwards. Success looks like: your top hip stays stacked over the bottom one. If you have to roll back to open further, you have gone as far as it goes. 3x15 each side.

blocks.why: Sideways power, first and on its own, while fresh: a jump needs clear floor and a partner takes it. This is the only sideways work in the week, and every other lift here drives straight up and down. It was in the programme until 2026-08-31 and was deleted by mistake when the week was rebuilt, the day after he last performed it. Deng 2024 reports small to moderate effects across four outcomes at 2 to 3 plyometric sessions a week, which is why this is on two days and is not the point of either.

blocks.label: Single Leg

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: BB Back Squat
alts.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

exercises.name: DB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there, like you are pinching a pencil between them. Breathe in, lower the dumbbells until you feel a good stretch across the chest, PAUSE for one second so there is no bounce, then press up and breathe out. The dumbbells travel slightly toward each other at the top but do not clang. ADDED 2026-08-22, after he reported feeling this mostly in the triceps and the front of the shoulder: that is usually where the dumbbells are travelling, not how hard you are pushing. Two things to try. Before the first rep, pull your shoulder blades DOWN and TOGETHER into the bench and keep them pinned there the whole set, so your chest is the highest point and the shoulders cannot roll forward. Then press over your LOWER chest, not your collarbone: at the bottom the dumbbells should be beside your nipples with your elbows about halfway between tucked-in and straight-out, and at the top they finish above the same spot rather than drifting toward your face. Success looks like: at the bottom you feel a stretch across the chest, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder. This is standard coaching practice, not a trial finding.
exercises.whyHere: DB Bench Press goes in the rest because the Bulgarian Split Squat does not use the chest.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: Your second press of the week, moderate rather than heavy: Tuesday is the day the bench gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Lean your chest forward to bias the chest. Enough counterweight for 8 clean reps. You had 5 strict dips in May, so this is trackable.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat, dumbbells. About 30 degrees, which is one or two notches, not half way up. More work for the top of the chest and the front of the shoulder, less for the middle and lower chest. Your note #31 asked what the difference is: neither is better, they are different halves of the same muscle, and the steeper you go the more the shoulder takes over. Success looks like: you feel it across your collarbone rather than under your nipple line. If your shoulders are doing all of it, lower the bench a notch. If you are doing this instead of flat, SWAP TO IT on the card so your log says what you actually pressed.

alts.name: Chest Fly Machine
alts.cue: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.

blocks.why: The single-leg pattern leading a block, which it has never done. It is half of what lower-body strength means and every one of its sets sits in an accessory block today. DB Bench Press goes in the rest because the Bulgarian Split Squat does not use the chest.

blocks.label: Main Lift: BB Row

exercises.name: BB Row
exercises.cue: This has been stuck at 165 lb since May because it always came fifth, when you were already cooked. It now leads the day, so it should move. Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS backward past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Your torso does not move: if you are standing up a little to help the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench, dumbbells hanging. The bench removes the lower back entirely, so nothing can cheat. Good on a day the RDLs left your back tired.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-Up
alts.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Lunge
exercises.cue: This is the sideways movement you asked for, and it is loaded on purpose: unweighted band walks were shown to do little. Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Step wide to the LEFT and sit back into that left hip, keeping the right leg straight with the foot flat. Both feet stay pointing forward the whole time. Push off the left foot to come back. You should feel a stretch on the inside of the straight leg and work in the bent leg's hip. Start with a light dumbbell and a small step, then widen the step before you add weight.
exercises.whyHere: DB Lateral Lunge goes in the rest because the BB Row does not use the legs.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

blocks.why: The heavy horizontal pull, 185 lb over 25 logged sets, every one completed. DB Lateral Lunge goes in the rest because the BB Row does not use the legs.

blocks.label: Trunk and Calves

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the bench, between press sets. Your example, and it is the pairing that always worked. On your back, arms straight up at the ceiling, knees bent up over your hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and keep it there: that is the entire exercise. Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathe out as they go. Stop the moment your lower back lifts off the floor, even if the leg is nowhere near down. Come back and swap sides.

alts.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
alts.cue: On the floor. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, put it back, tap with the other. Success looks like: your hips do not rock side to side as the hand leaves the floor. If they rock, put your feet wider. 3x10 each side.

alts.name: Hanging Knee Raise
alts.cue: Hang from the pull-up bar on top of the rack with your arms straight and your feet clear of the floor. Bring both knees up towards your chest until your thighs pass level, then lower them under control until your legs are straight again. Success looks like: you come to a stop at the bottom before the next rep, so every one starts from still rather than from a swing. If you are swinging, do fewer. THIS CUE IS A DRAFT: it was written for you rather than taken off a published page, and nobody has read it standing at the bar. Say what it should say.

alts.name: Hollow Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

exercises.name: DB Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Standing on the floor in the rest between lunge sets, a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides. Feet about hip width. Push all the way up onto your toes, as high as you can go, and hold for one second at the top. Then lower slowly, about three seconds down, until your heels touch the floor and you feel a stretch through the back of the calf. Success looks like: you can hold the top position still for a second without wobbling, and the slow way down is what you feel most. If you cannot hold the top, the dumbbells are too heavy. This is the flat-floor version, so the stretch at the bottom is smaller than on the machine; that is the trade for it costing you no walk.
exercises.whyHere: DB Calf Raise goes in the rest because the Dead Bug does not use the calves.

alts.name: Machine Calf Raise
alts.cue: On the standing calf machine. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

blocks.why: The trunk, which carries the least direct work of any region here, and the calves, which nothing else in the week trains twice. DB Calf Raise goes in the rest because the Dead Bug does not use the calves.

blocks.label: Hinge

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge, the one we progress. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar stays touching your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and then FREEZE them, then push your hips backward toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and snap the hips forward to stand up, breathing out at the top. If your lower back rounds you have gone too far down. STRAPS, because you asked on 18 August: yes, use them, and they will not cost you anything here. Do the first warm-up set with bare hands so you keep noticing what your grip is doing, then strap up for all four working sets. The hamstrings are what this lift is for, and stopping a set because the bar is slipping out of your fingers trains neither. Your grip is not being neglected either: the Farmer Carry on Friday and the Suitcase Carry on Monday are both held bare-handed and that is where grip is meant to be worked. This is standard coaching practice rather than something a trial has tested, so it is a convention, not evidence.

open.q: Standing in the rack with a loaded bar: could another member still use the pull-up bar above you? If they cannot, hanging knee raises can ride in your RDL rest. Can they?
Do you want hanging knee raises in the RDL rest? It is 3 more ab sets on top of the 6 direct ones already here, or I can move work already in the week into that gap and add nothing. Which?

alts.name: Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: Has sat at 40 lb since May, so this time the weight moves, not just the reps. One dumbbell in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and frozen. Push the hip backward and let the free leg extend straight behind you like a see-saw, keeping your hips square to the floor: the back hip must not open toward the ceiling. Go until you feel the hamstring stretch, then stand and squeeze. Slow. Touch the bench with your free toe if you lose balance.

alts.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: KB Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

exercises.name: DB Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging by your sides, palms facing IN toward your thighs and STAYING that way the whole rep: that is what makes it a hammer curl instead of a normal curl. Pin your elbows against your ribs. Bend the elbow and bring the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, then lower it all the way until the arm is straight. Success looks like: your elbows have not travelled forward and your body has not swung to start the rep. If it swings, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.
exercises.whyHere: DB Hammer Curl goes in the rest because the BB Romanian Deadlift does not use the arms.

alts.name: DB Biceps Curl
alts.cue: Standing, dumbbells, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.

alts.name: Cable Curl
alts.cue: Low cable with a straight or EZ attachment. The cable keeps tension on the muscle at every point, including the top where dumbbells go light. 3x12.

alts.name: Incline DB Curl
alts.cue: A dumbbell in each hand on the incline bench. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

alts.name: Kettlebell Curl
alts.cue: A kettlebell in each hand by the handle, same elbow-pinned curl. The weight hangs behind your hand, which makes the top half harder.

blocks.why: The second hinge of the week, moderate, so the heavy one lands on its own day. DB Hammer Curl goes in the rest because the BB Romanian Deadlift does not use the arms.
